key_insight: Introduce a lightweight metacognitive layer for training-free, foundation-model VLN agents that monitors exploration, diagnoses failures, and adaptively changes strategy—dramatically reducing wandering and redundant revisits without additional model training.
problem_solved: Addresses inefficient exploration in vision-language navigation caused by greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory, which leads to local oscillation and redundant revisiting.
method: Metacognitive monitoring: compute online metrics (progress, confidence, revisit counts) to detect failures or stagnation during exploration.
Adaptive strategy selection: dynamically re-rank/frontier-score candidate actions and switch exploration behaviors (exploit vs. explore) based on diagnostic signals—no extra model training required.
Active spatial memory: maintain and update a memory that penalizes oscillation and prioritizes informative, novel frontiers to guide more efficient paths.
impact: Makes foundation-model VLN agents far more sample- and time-efficient by reducing wasted motion and improving success rates—provides a modular, training-free upgrade that practitioners can plug into existing systems.

paper_title: Stop Wandering: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation via Metacognitive Reasoning
paper_authors: Xueying Li, Feng Lyu, Hao Wu, Mingliu Liu, Jia-Nan Liu
